title: The Wise Men of Chelm and the White Snow
summary: On Friday the first snow falls on Chelm, white and beautiful, and Yokel the shammes has to go out and call everyone to Shabbat. But how can he walk without stepping on the snow? The wise men come up with one solution after another, each sillier than the last, until there's a tower of tables wobbling up to the clouds... and only little Gitele knows what to do. A rhyming story based on a folk tale of the Wise Men of Chelm.
pages:
On Friday in Chelm the first snow came down,
white as sugar on every roof and window in town.
Yokel the shammes took his hammer to knock "Shabbat!" — all ready to go,
but all the wise men shouted, "Oy, oy! Don't step on the white snow!"

The wise men sat, and they thought, and they scratched their beards slow,
until Reb Kalman jumped up: "I've got a little idea, you know!"
So Yokel tiptoed, tip-tip, as light as a feather can be,
but behind him — holes, holes, from his house to the end, as far as you could see!
"Oy, oy! Don't step on the white snow!"

"Stilts!" cried Reb Zalman. "Tall wooden legs, long and high!
Yokel will stride way up there, by the roofs and the chimneys in the sky!"
Yokel wobbled left, then right... CRASH! BOOM!
And deep pits were left in the snow everywhere, like the craters on the moon!
"Oy, oy! Don't step on the white snow!"

Reb Shmerel, the wisest in Chelm, smiled a small, knowing smile:
"Yokel won't walk at all! Yokel will stand on a table — in style!
And four strong men will lift the table — hop! — up high,
and Yokel will ride through town like a groom at a grand wedding passing by!"

Four strong men lifted the table: "One, two... HOP!"
and Yokel stood up on top, banging his hammer like a drum — bop-bop!
Tok-tok on every shutter: "Shabbat! Close up! Shabbat in town!"
And the wise men clapped: "What an idea! What a brilliant idea — it deserves a crown!"

But little Gitele, in her red scarf, pointed a finger and counted some more:
"A leg, and a leg... one, two, three, four...
five, six, seven, eight! Eight legs instead of two!"
And the wise men panicked and threw up their hands to the sky — oh, what to do?
"Oy, oy! Don't step on the white snow!"

Reb Shmerel didn't panic: "Very simple! Another table, a bigger one,
and eight men will lift the four, and Yokel, and everyone!"
"And for the eight — sixteen!" "And more... and more... and more!"
until all of Chelm was hauling a tower of tables — wobbling, and taller than ever before!

The tower swayed to the right... and to the left... so slow, so slow...
and... PLOOF! All of Chelm tumbled at once into the soft white snow.
Old men and tables, boots and coats — one great big pile, all round,
and Yokel sat on top with his hammer, like a cherry on a round cake — crowned!

Gitele laughed: "Now there's nothing left to protect, you see!
All the snow's been stepped on — there's not a single spot that's hole-free!"
So Yokel got up, shook off his coat, and ran, tok-tok, down every street:
"Shabbat! Shabbat in Chelm!" — and all the children jumped in the snow. What a treat!

And on Shabbat eve, when the candles were lit and the challah waited on the table,
new snow fell on Chelm, white as sugar, on every window and every gable.
The wise men peeked out, and Gitele peeked, and all of Chelm, big and small, in a row:
"Oy, oy! Don't step on the white snow!"
